passages.text: Nevertheless, there will be no more gloom for those in distress. In the past He humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future He will honor the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject of this passage.
God once humbled the land of Zebulun.
God once humbled the land of Naphtali.
God brought distress to these places in the past.
God will not bring gloom to those in distress now.
God will honor the Way of the Sea in the future.
God will honor the land beyond the Jordan.
God will honor Galilee of the nations.
People walked in darkness.
These people saw a great light.
Some people lived in the land of the shadow of death.
A light has dawned on them.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן הֵקַ֞ל אַ֤רְצָה זְבֻלוּן֙ וְאַ֣רְצָה נַפְתָּלִ֔י וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַיָּם֙ עֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן גְּלִ֖יל הַגּוֹיִֽם׃ הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ רָא֖וּ א֣וֹר גָּד֑וֹל יֹשְׁבֵי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ צַלְמָ֔וֶת א֖וֹר נָגַ֥הּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: You have enlarged the nation and increased its joy. The people rejoice before You as they rejoice at harvest time, as men rejoice in dividing the plunder.
passages.sermon:
God enlarged the nation.
God increased the nation’s joy.
The people rejoice before God.
They rejoice as people rejoice at harvest time.
They rejoice as people rejoice when they divide plunder.
passages.original: הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי לֹא הִגְדַּ֣לְתָּ הַשִּׂמְחָ֑ה שָׂמְח֤וּ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ כְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת בַּקָּצִ֔יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגִ֖ילוּ בְּחַלְּקָ֥ם שָׁלָֽל׃

passages.text: For as in the day of Midian You have shattered the yoke of their burden, the bar across their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God broke the yoke that burdened the people.
God removed the bar that pressed on their shoulders.
God shattered the rod used by their oppressor.
God did this as He did in the day of Midian.
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ אֶת־ עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ וְאֵת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה שִׁכְמ֔וֹ שֵׁ֖בֶט הַנֹּגֵ֣שׂ בּ֑וֹ הַחִתֹּ֖תָ כְּי֥וֹם מִדְיָֽן׃

passages.text: For every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes what happens after God brings victory and peace to His people.
God removes the tools and signs of war.
Every boot that soldiers used in battle will be destroyed.
Every garment stained with blood will be destroyed.
People will burn these things in the fire.
They will use them as fuel for the flames.
There will be no more need for these things.
God brings an end to war and violence.
passages.original: כִּ֤י כָל־ סְאוֹן֙ סֹאֵ֣ן בְּרַ֔עַשׁ וְשִׂמְלָ֖ה מְגוֹלָלָ֣ה בְדָמִ֑ים וְהָיְתָ֥ה לִשְׂרֵפָ֖ה מַאֲכֹ֥לֶת אֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
passages.sermon:
God promised to send someone special to us.
A child is born for us.
A son is given to us.
This son will rule.
He will carry the government on His shoulders.
People will call Him Wonderful Counselor.
People will call Him Mighty God.
People will call Him Everlasting Father.
People will call Him Prince of Peace.
passages.original: כִּי־ יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד־ לָ֗נוּ בֵּ֚ן נִתַּן־ לָ֔נוּ וַתְּהִ֥י הַמִּשְׂרָ֖ה עַל־ שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִיעַ֖ד שַׂר־ שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness from that time and forevermore. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
passages.sermon:
God promised a ruler for His people.
This ruler will have a government that always grows.
His peace will never end.
He will sit on David’s throne.
He will rule over David’s kingdom.
He will make the kingdom strong.
He will support it with justice.
He will support it with righteousness.
He will do this from that time and forever.
The LORD of Hosts is very zealous.
The LORD of Hosts will make this happen.
passages.original: לְםַרְבֵּה הַמִּשְׂרָ֜ה וּלְשָׁל֣וֹם אֵֽין־ קֵ֗ץ עַל־ כִּסֵּ֤א דָוִד֙ וְעַל־ מַמְלַכְתּ֔וֹ לְהָכִ֤ין אֹתָהּ֙ וּֽלְסַעֲדָ֔הּ בְּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּבִצְדָקָ֑ה מֵעַתָּה֙ וְעַד־ עוֹלָ֔ם קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־ זֹּֽאת׃ס

passages.text: The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the subject.
The Lord sent a message.
The Lord sent this message against Jacob.
This message has fallen upon Israel.
passages.original: דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְנָפַ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: All the people will know it— Ephraim and the dwellers of Samaria. With pride and arrogance of heart they will say: “The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with finished stone; the sycamores have been felled, but we will replace them with cedars.”
passages.sermon:
All the people will know this.
Ephraim will know it.
The people who live in Samaria will know it.
They will speak with pride.
They will speak with arrogance in their hearts.
They will say, “The bricks have fallen.
But we will build again with cut stone.
The sycamore trees have been cut down.
But we will put cedars in their place.”
passages.original: וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן בְּגַאֲוָ֛ה וּבְגֹ֥דֶל לֵבָ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר׃ לְבֵנִ֥ים נָפָ֖לוּ וְגָזִ֣ית נִבְנֶ֑ה שִׁקְמִ֣ים גֻּדָּ֔עוּ וַאֲרָזִ֖ים נַחֲלִֽיף׃

passages.text: The LORD has raised up the foes of Rezin against him and joined his enemies together.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD acts with power.
The LORD raised up the enemies of Rezin.
The LORD brought these enemies against him.
The LORD joined his enemies together.
passages.original: וַיְשַׂגֵּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ צָרֵ֥י רְצִ֖ין עָלָ֑יו וְאֶת־ אֹיְבָ֖יו יְסַכְסֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Aram from the east and Philistia from the west have devoured Israel with open mouths. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
passages.sermon:
Aram attacked Israel from the east.
Philistia attacked Israel from the west.
Aram and Philistia devoured Israel.
They attacked Israel with open mouths.
God saw all this.
God’s anger did not turn away.
God’s hand remained upraised.
passages.original: אֲרָ֣ם מִקֶּ֗דֶם וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ מֵֽאָח֔וֹר וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל־ פֶּ֑ה בְּכָל־ זֹאת֙ לֹא־ שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃

passages.text: But the people did not return to Him who struck them; they did not seek the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon: The people did not return to God.\r\nGod had struck them.\r\nThe people did not seek the LORD of Hosts.
passages.original: וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא־ שָׁ֖ב עַד־ הַמַּכֵּ֑הוּ וְאֶת־ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃ס

passages.text: So the LORD will cut off Israel’s head and tail, both palm branch and reed in a single day.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will act against Israel.
The LORD will cut off Israel’s head.
The LORD will cut off Israel’s tail.
The LORD will cut off the palm branch.
The LORD will cut off the reed.
The LORD will do all this in a single day.
passages.original: וַיַּכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֗ל רֹ֧אשׁ וְזָנָ֛ב כִּפָּ֥ה וְאַגְמ֖וֹן י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: The head is the elder and honorable man, and the tail is the prophet who teaches lies.
passages.sermon:
The head means the elder.
The elder is an honorable man.
The tail means the prophet.
The prophet teaches lies.
passages.original: זָקֵ֥ן וּנְשׂוּא־ פָנִ֖ים ה֣וּא הָרֹ֑אשׁ וְנָבִ֥יא מֽוֹרֶה־ שֶּׁ֖קֶר ה֥וּא הַזָּנָֽב׃

passages.text: For those who guide this people mislead them, and those they mislead are swallowed up.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of this people guide them.
These leaders mislead the people.
The people who follow them are led astray.
Those who are misled are destroyed.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ מְאַשְּׁרֵ֥י הָֽעָם־ הַזֶּ֖ה מַתְעִ֑ים וּמְאֻשָּׁרָ֖יו מְבֻלָּעִֽים׃

passages.text: Therefore the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men; He has no compassion on their fatherless and widows. For every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the one who judges the people.
The Lord does not take pleasure in their young men.
The Lord does not have compassion on their orphans.
The Lord does not have compassion on their widows.
Every person among them is godless.
Every person among them is wicked.
Every mouth speaks foolishness.
Even after all this, the Lord’s anger does not turn away.
The Lord’s hand is still raised against them.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֨ן עַל־ בַּחוּרָ֜יו לֹֽא־ יִשְׂמַ֣ח׀ אֲדֹנָ֗י וְאֶת־ יְתֹמָ֤יו וְאֶת־ אַלְמְנֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔ם כִּ֤י כֻלּוֹ֙ חָנֵ֣ף וּמֵרַ֔ע וְכָל־ פֶּ֖ה דֹּבֵ֣ר נְבָלָ֑ה בְּכָל־ זֹאת֙ לֹא־ שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃

passages.text: For wickedness burns like a fire that consumes the thorns and briers and kindles the forest thickets which roll upward in billows of smoke.
passages.sermon:
Wickedness acts like a fire.
Wickedness burns strongly.
Wickedness destroys everything in its path.
Wickedness consumes thorns and briers.
Wickedness sets the forest thickets on fire.
Smoke rises in great billows from the burning.
The smoke rolls upward, showing the destruction.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ בָעֲרָ֤ה כָאֵשׁ֙ רִשְׁעָ֔ה שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תֹּאכֵ֑ל וַתִּצַּת֙ בְּסִֽבְכֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר וַיִּֽתְאַבְּכ֖וּ גֵּא֥וּת עָשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people are fuel for the fire. No man even spares his brother.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is angry.
His wrath burns against the land.
The land becomes scorched.
The people become fuel for the fire.
No one shows mercy to his brother.
passages.original: בְּעֶבְרַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת נֶעְתַּ֣ם אָ֑רֶץ וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמַאֲכֹ֣לֶת אֵ֔שׁ אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א יַחְמֹֽלוּ׃

passages.text: They carve out what is on the right, but they are still hungry; they eat what is on the left, but they are still not satisfied. Each one devours the flesh of his own offspring.
passages.sermon:
The people act with greed and violence.
They take from the right side.
They remain hungry.
They eat from the left side.
They are still not satisfied.
Each person devours the flesh of his own child.
passages.original: וַיִּגְזֹ֤ר עַל־ יָמִין֙ וְרָעֵ֔ב וַיֹּ֥אכַל עַל־ שְׂמֹ֖אול וְלֹ֣א שָׂבֵ֑עוּ אִ֥ישׁ בְּשַׂר־ זְרֹע֖וֹ יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
passages.sermon:
Manasseh attacks Ephraim.
Ephraim attacks Manasseh.
Both tribes fight each other.
Together, they turn against Judah.
The Lord is angry.
His anger does not turn away.
His hand is still raised to strike.
passages.original: מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אֶת־ אֶפְרַ֗יִם וְאֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶת־ מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יַחְדָּ֥ו הֵ֖מָּה עַל־ יְהוּדָ֑ה בְּכָל־ זֹאת֙ לֹא־ שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ס
